name: Marketing
tagline: Draft campaign content and collect results from the tools your team uses.

useCases.title: Campaign planning
useCases.description: Turn a one-line goal into a multi-channel plan: messaging, channel mix, calendar, and draft assets ready to edit.

useCases.title: One post, many formats
useCases.description: Turn one blog post into a thread, a LinkedIn post, three ad variations, and an email, in your brand voice.

useCases.title: Social scheduling
useCases.description: Draft a week of posts and queue them into your scheduler or post them to Slack for sign-off first.

useCases.title: Competitor and trend research
useCases.description: Browse the web for competitor launches and trending angles, then summarize the takeaways into a brief.

useCases.title: Performance recaps
useCases.description: Pull last week's numbers, compare against goals, and write a plain-English recap with what to do next.

useCases.title: Repurposing long-form
useCases.description: Take a webinar transcript or report and cut it into clips, quotes, captions, and a recap newsletter.

faq.q: Can agents post and update tools?
faq.a: Yes. Through Connections, agents sign in to apps like Slack, Notion, and your social scheduler and act there. You can require sign-off first.
Add your brand guidelines, tone docs, and past campaigns to a Space. Drafts reference your own material, so voice stays consistent and you can check the source.

faq.q: How do we keep AI costs down?
faq.a: Set budgets per agent in the Gateway, and route drafts to a free local model and the high-stakes piece to a stronger one. You see the spend and the history of routed calls.
